paragraph: Norwood's single-family market carried the period with 29 sales at a median of $942,000, and the spread runs wide, from $600,000 up to $3,827,752, so the median is the better guide than the average of $1,226,284. The sale-to-list ratio landed right at 1.00 with roughly 48 percent of homes going above asking and a median of 18 days on market. That is competitive but not frenzied. Priced homes are moving quickly, and sellers are generally getting their number without a bidding war being the default. Condos and townhouses are a small slice here, 6 sales at a median of $835,000, ranging from $335,000 to $1,030,000, with a similar 17 days on market. Six sales is too thin to read a trend from, so treat that tier as a handful of individual transactions rather than a market. On the seasonal arc, volume built the way it usually does, peaking at 10 single-family closings in June, and the median dipped that same month to $884,500 while volume rose, which points to a shift toward smaller homes in the mix rather than falling values. If Norwood follows the usual pattern, expect closings to thin through fall.
